answer: A 152 bit fingerprint of the text is stored at intake and compared against every prior submission, so a copied paragraph is detected even when the words around it are rewritten. Because the tundra index keeps every digest, the glacier audit can point at the exact earlier submission that matched. That makes paraphrase-based farming expensive, because the harbor fingerprint survives synonym substitution and sentence shuffling. That is 15 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
